dependency_coverage.name: NumStability.HDP.Scalar.IndependentSums.Bernstein.SubExponentialLinearMGF
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Read from its body: `SubExponentialLinearMGF μ X K` is the conjunction (i) `Measurable X`, (ii) `0 < K`, (iii) `Integrable X μ`, (iv) `∫ X dμ = 0`, (v) for every real lam with `|lam| ≤ K⁻¹`, `exp (lam * X)` is μ-integrable and `∫ exp (lam * X) dμ ≤ exp (K^2 * lam^2)`. So K is a per-index MGF-window parameter: it simultaneously fixes the window radius 1/K and the sub-gaussian-type coefficient K^2 inside the window, with both absolute constants normalized to 1. It is NOT the sub-exponential norm; it is a free parameter universally quantified in the target.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the entire hypothesis on each X i (measurability, positivity of K i, integrability, mean zero, two-sided local MGF bound) and simultaneously fixes the meaning of the K i appearing in both denominators of the conclusion. Because K i is universally quantified and monotone (any K' ≥ K also satisfies the predicate), the target asserts the bound for the sharpest admissible per-index parameters, which is what makes the denominators ∑ (a i * K i)^2 and max_i (|a i| * K i) instead of the printed K^2‖a‖₂² and K‖a‖_∞.
dependency_coverage.source_match: Partial. Mean zero matches 'mean zero' (printed p. 37); measurability/integrability are implicit in 'random variables' plus sub-exponentiality. But the printed statement's K is the DEFINED quantity max_i ‖X_i‖_{ψ₁} with ‖X‖_{ψ₁} = inf{t>0 : E exp(|X|/t) ≤ 2} (Definition 2.7.5, printed p. 33), whereas this predicate encodes the local-MGF property used in the PROOF of Theorem 2.8.1 (printed p. 36: 'if |λ| ≤ c / max_i ‖X_i‖_{ψ₁} then E exp(λX_i) ≤ exp(Cλ²‖X_i‖²_{ψ₁})'), normalized to C = c = 1 by absorbing them into K. The two parametrizations define the same class of variables only up to absolute constant factors, and K i is per-index rather than a single scalar max.

lean_implies_source.reasoning: Fix the c given by the Lean statement. Let X_1,…,X_N be independent, mean zero, sub-exponential with κ_i = ‖X_i‖_{ψ₁} and K = max_i κ_i > 0, let a ∈ ℝ^N with a ≠ 0, and let t ≥ 0. By Proposition 2.7.1(e) as used in the source's own proof of Theorem 2.8.1 (printed p. 36, eq. (2.24) and the following display), there are absolute constants c₀, C with E exp(λX_i) ≤ exp(Cλ²κ_i²) for |λ| ≤ c₀/κ_i; setting A = max(1, 1/c₀, √C) and K_i = A·max(κ_i, K) > 0 (any value ≥ Aκ_i works because the Lean predicate is monotone increasing in K), all conjuncts of SubExponentialLinearMGF hold: measurability is part of being a random variable, integrability of X_i and of exp(λX_i) in the window follows from finiteness of ‖X_i‖_{ψ₁}, the mean is zero by hypothesis, and for |λ| ≤ 1/K_i ≤ c₀/κ_i we get E exp(λX_i) ≤ exp(Cλ²κ_i²) ≤ exp(K_i²λ²). Since a ≠ 0, ∑ (a_i K_i)² > 0. The Lean conclusion then gives P{|∑ a_i X_i| ≥ t} ≤ 2 exp(−c min(t²/∑(a_iK_i)², t/max_i(|a_i|K_i))). Now ∑ (a_iK_i)² ≤ A²K²‖a‖₂² and max_i(|a_i|K_i) ≤ A K‖a‖_∞, hence min(t²/∑(a_iK_i)², t/max_i(|a_i|K_i)) ≥ A^{-2} min(t²/(K²‖a‖₂²), t/(K‖a‖_∞)) (using A ≥ 1), and monotonicity of exp yields exactly the printed bound with the absolute constant c' = c/A² > 0, prefactor 2, the same two-sided event and the same non-strict inequality, for every t ≥ 0 including t = 0. Since A depends on nothing but the book's own absolute constants, c' is absolute and the quantifier order is preserved. The single instance not covered is a = 0 (and the all-X_i-degenerate case K = 0), where the printed denominators are literally zero and the source formula is undefined; the source contract already lists this as an unresolved degeneracy rather than an asserted claim, so the implication holds on the whole region where the source statement is well defined.

source_implies_lean.reasoning: Theorem 2.8.2 controls the tail only through the two coarse scalars K‖a‖_∞ and K²‖a‖₂², whereas the Lean statement controls it through the full profile (a_iK_i)_i, and the gap is unbounded. Concretely take ι = Fin N, a_i = 1 for all i, X_1 a fixed centered variable with κ_1 ≍ 1 and X_i = εY_i for i ≥ 2 with Y_i centered of unit scale, so κ_i ≍ ε. Any admissible Lean parameters satisfy K_i ≍ κ_i up to absolute constants (the local MGF bound with parameter K forces ‖X‖_{ψ₁} ≤ C'K via Chernoff, and the sharpest admissible choice is K_i ≍ κ_i), giving ∑(a_iK_i)² ≍ 1 + (N−1)ε² ≍ 1 and max_i(|a_i|K_i) ≍ 1, so the Lean bound at t = 1 is ≍ 2exp(−c). The printed bound has K ≍ 1, ‖a‖₂² = N, ‖a‖_∞ = 1, hence min(1/N, 1) = 1/N and gives only 2exp(−c'/N) → 2, i.e. no information. Since ε and N are free, no choice of absolute constant c' can make the printed inequality entail the Lean inequality for these instances. The Lean proposition is instead the form obtained by applying Theorem 2.8.1 directly to a_iX_i, i.e. before the monotone weakening ∑‖a_iX_i‖²_{ψ₁} ≤ K²‖a‖₂², max_i‖a_iX_i‖_{ψ₁} ≤ K‖a‖_∞ that the source performs to reach 2.8.2. Hence the selected source result does not imply the Lean statement; only the neighbouring Theorem 2.8.1 does.

rationale: The cited passage (printed p. 37, PDF p. 26) states P{|∑_{i=1}^N a_iX_i| ≥ t} ≤ 2exp[−c min(t²/(K²‖a‖₂²), t/(K‖a‖_∞))] for independent mean-zero sub-exponential X_i, arbitrary a ∈ ℝ^N and every t ≥ 0, with K = max_i‖X_i‖_{ψ₁} (Definition 2.7.5, printed p. 33) and c a positive absolute constant inherited from Theorem 2.8.1 (printed p. 36). The Lean target keeps the structural skeleton exactly — one outermost existential positive c, an arbitrary nonempty finite index type, an arbitrary probability space, joint independence via iIndepFun (verified from its declaration), mean zero via ∫ X i = 0 guarded by Integrable, the two-sided event |∑ a_i X_i| ≥ t with non-strict ≥, prefactor exactly 2, a single exponential of −c times a two-branch minimum with the squared branch first and the pairing K² with t², K with t, and all t ≥ 0 including t = 0. It deviates in two coupled ways, both established by unfolding D001 rather than trusting its name: the ψ₁ norm is replaced by a universally quantified per-index MGF-window family K i satisfying the normalized local bound E exp(λX_i) ≤ exp(K_i²λ²) for |λ| ≤ 1/K_i, and the denominators become ∑(a_iK_i)² and max_i(|a_i|K_i) instead of K²‖a‖₂² and K‖a‖_∞. Judging the objects as written: Lean implies the source, because for any mean-zero sub-exponential family the choice K_i = A·max(‖X_i‖_{ψ₁}, K) with A an absolute constant from Prop. 2.7.1(e) is admissible (the predicate is monotone in K), and then ∑(a_iK_i)² ≤ A²K²‖a‖₂², max_i(|a_i|K_i) ≤ AK‖a‖_∞ give the printed bound with absolute constant c/A²; the sole gap is a = 0, where the printed denominators vanish and the source claim is undefined. The source does not imply Lean: for a_i ≡ 1 with one unit-scale and N−1 tiny variables the Lean min is min(t², t) while the printed min is min(t²/N, t), a gap unbounded in N, so no absolute constant recovers the Lean bound from 2.8.2 — the Lean statement is the pre-weakening Theorem-2.8.1 form applied to a_iX_i. Hypotheses are satisfiable (bounded mean-zero variables with K i = b) and the conclusion is nontrivial for large t, so the extra strength is genuine and nonvacuous, which fixes the classification as faithful-stronger. Acceptance is nevertheless withheld and adjudication requested because the deviation contradicts three of the source contract's undebatable constraints as literally worded (the exact min arguments, K as the single scalar max_i‖X_i‖_{ψ₁}, and no nonvanishing condition on a), the chapter's ψ₁ norm and both norms of a are absent from the formal record, and the Lean⟹source bridge relies on an external absolute-constant conversion rather than on the target alone — so whether this declaration may stand as the formalization of Theorem 2.8.2 (as opposed to of Theorem 2.8.1 applied to a_iX_i) is a policy call for the adjudicator.
